source_text: Δεῖ οὖν ἡμᾶς περὶ τῶν ἐνεστώτων ἐπιπολὺ ἐραυνῶντας ἐκζητεῖν τὰ δυνάμενα ἡμᾶς σώζειν. φύγωμεν οὑν τελείως ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἔργων τῆς ἀνομίας, μήποτε καταλάβῃ ἡμᾶς τὰ ἔργα τῆς ἀνομίας: καὶ μισήσωμεν τὴν πλάνην τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ, ἵνα εἰς τὸν μέλλοντα ἀγαπηθῶμεν. μὴ δῶμεν τῇ ἑαυτῶν ψυχῇ ἄνεσιν, ὥστε ἔχειν αὐτὴν ἐξουσίαν μετὰ ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ πονηρῶν συντρέχειν, μήποτε ὁμοιωθῶμεν αὐτοῖς. τὸ τέλειον σκάνδαλον ἤγγικεν, περὶ οὖ γέγραπται, ὡς Ἐνὼχ λέγει. Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὁ δεσπότης συντέτμηκεν τοὺς καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ἡμέρας, ἵνα ταχύνῃ ὁ ἠγαπημένος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν κληρονομίαν ἥξῃ, λέγει δὲ οὕτως καὶ ὁ προφήτης: Βασιλεῖαι δέκα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς βασιλεύσουσιν, καὶ ἐξαναστήσεται ὄπισθεν μικρὸς βασιλεύς, ὃς ταπεινώσει τρεῖς ὑφ̓ ἓν τῶν βασιλέων. ὁμοίως περὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ λέγει Δανιήλ: Καὶ εἶδον τὸ τέταρτον θηρίον τὸ πονηρὸν καὶ ἰσχυρὸν καὶ χαλεπώτερον παρὰ πάντα τὰ θηρία τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ ὡς ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἀνέτειλεν δέκα κέρατα, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μικρὸν κέρας παραφυάδιον, καὶ ὡς ἐταπείνωσεν ὑφ̓ ἓν τρία τῶν μεγάλων κεράτων. συνιέναι οὖν ὀφείλετε. ἔτι δὲ καὶ τοῦτο ἐρωτῶ ὑμᾶς ὡς εἶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ὤν, ἰδίως δὲ καὶ πάντας ἀγαπῶν ὑπὲρ τὴν ψυχήν μου, προσέχειν νῦν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ μὴ ὁμοιοῦσθαί τισιν ἐπισωρεύοντας ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν λέγοντας, ὅτι ἡ διαθήκη ἐκείνων καὶ ἡμῶν. ἡμῶν μέν: ἀλλ’ ἐκεῖνοι οὕτως εἰς τέλος ἀπώλεσαν αὐτὴν λαβόντος ἤδη τοῦ Μωϋσέως. λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή: Καὶ ἦν Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ ὄρει νηστεύων ἡμέρας τεσσαράκοντα καὶ νύκτας τεσσαράκοντα, καὶ ἔλαβεν τὴν διαθήκην ἀπὸ τοῦ κυρίου, πλάκας λιθίνας γεγραμμένας τῷ δακτύλῳ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ κυρίου. ἀλλὰ ἐπιστραφέντες ἐπὶ τὰ εἴδωλα ἀπώλεσαν αὐτήν. λέγει γὰρ οὕτως κύριος. Μωϋσῆ Μωϋσῆ, κατάβηθι τὸ τάχος, ὅτι ἠνόμησεν ὁ λαός σου, οὓς ἐξήγαγες ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, καὶ συνῆκεν Μωϋσῆς καὶ ἔριψεν τὰς δύο πλάκας ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ: καὶ συνετρίβη αὐτῶν ἡ διαθήκη, ἵνα ἡ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου Ἰησοῦ ἐγκατασφραγισθῇ εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἡμῶν ἐν ἐλπίδι τῆς πίστεως αὐτοῦ. πολλὰ δὲ θέλων γράφειν, οὐχ ὡς διδάσκαλος, ἀλλ’ ὡς πρέπει ἀγαπῶντι ἀφ̓ ὧν ἔχομεν μὴ ἐλλείπειν, γράφειν ἐσπούδασα, περίψημα ὑμῶν. διὸ προσέχωμεν ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις: οὐδὲν γὰρ ὠφελήσει ἡμᾶς ὁ πᾶς χρόνος τῆς πίστεως ἡμῶν, ἐὰν μὴ νῦν ἐν τῷ ἀνόμῳ καιρῷ καὶ τοῖς μέλλουσιν σκανδάλοις, ὡς πρέπει υἱοῖς θεοῦ, ἀντιστῶμεν, ἵνα μὴ σχῇ παρείσδυσιν ὁ μέλας. φύγωμεν ἀπὸ πάσης ματαιότητος, μισήσωμεν τελείως τὰ ἔργα τῆς πονηρᾶς ὁδοῦ. μὴ καθ̓ ἑαυτοὺς ἐνδύνοντες μονάζετε ὡς ἤδη δεδικαιωμένοι, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ συνερχόμενοι συνζητεῖτε περὶ τοῦ κοινῇ συμφέροντος. λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή: Οὐαὶ οἱ συνετοὶ ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐνώπιαν ἑαυτῶν ἐπιστήμονες. γενώμεθα πνευματικοί, γενώμεθα ναὸς τέλειος τῷ θεῷ. ἐφ̓ ὅσον ἐστὶν ἐν ἡμῖν, μελετῶμεν τὸν φόβον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσειν ἀγωνιζώμεθα τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἐν τοῖς δικαιώμασιν αὐτοῦ εὐφρανθῶμεν. ὁ κύριος ἀπροσωπολήμπτως κρινεῖ τὸν κόσμον. ἕκαστος καθὼς ἐποίησεν κομιεῖται. ἐὰν ᾖ ἀγαθός, ἡ δικαιοσύνη αὐτοῦ προηγήσεται αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν ᾖ πονηρός, ὁ μισθὸς τῆς πονηρίας ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ: ἵνα μήποτε ἐπαναπαύομενοι ὡς κλητοὶ ἐπικαθυπνώσωμεν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἡμῶν, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄρχων λαβὼν τὴν καθ̓ ἡμῶν ἐξουσίαν ἀπώσηται ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ κυρίου. ἔτι δὲ κἀκεῖνο, ἀδελφοί μου, νοεῖτε: ὅταν βλέπετε μετὰ τηλικαῦτα σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γεγονότα ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, καὶ οὕτως ἐγκαταλελεῖφθαι αὐτούς: προσέχωμεν, μήποτε, ὡς γέγραπται, πολλοὶ κλητοί, ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοὶ εὑρεθῶμεν.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore it is necessary for us, inquiring thoroughly about the things that are present, to seek the things that are able to save us. Let us flee therefore completely from all the works of lawlessness, lest the works of lawlessness seize us: and let us hate the error of the present time, so that we may be loved for the future. Let us not give rest to our own soul, so that it may have authority to run with sinners and evil ones, lest we become like them. The perfect scandal has drawn near, about which it is written, as Enoch says. For the Lord has shortened the times and the days, so that his beloved may hasten and come to the inheritance, and the prophet says thus: Ten kingdoms will reign on the earth, and a small king will rise after them, who will humble three of the kings under one. Similarly, Daniel says about the same thing: And I saw the fourth beast, evil and strong and more savage than all the beasts of the sea, and as ten horns rose from it, and from them a small horn, a offshoot, and as it humbled three of the great horns under one. You ought to understand. And I ask you this also, as one of you, and especially loving all of you more than my own soul, to pay attention now to yourselves and not to be like some who are heaping up your sins, saying that their covenant is also ours. Ours, indeed: but they lost it in the end, having already received it from Moses. For the scripture says: And Moses was on the mountain, fasting forty days and forty nights, and he received the covenant from the Lord, stone tablets written with the finger of the Lord's hand. But they turned back to idols and lost it. For the Lord says: Moses, Moses, come down quickly, because your people, whom you led out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly, and Moses understood and threw the two tablets out of his hands: and their covenant was shattered, so that the covenant of the beloved Jesus may be sealed in our hearts in the hope of his faith. Although I wanted to write many things, not as a teacher, but as is fitting for one who loves, lest we be lacking in what we have, I have endeavored to write to you, for your sake. Therefore, let us pay attention in the last days: for all the time of our faith will not benefit us, if we do not now, in the lawless time and the coming scandals, stand as is fitting for sons of God, so that the evil one may not gain an advantage. Let us flee from all vanity, let us completely hate the works of the evil way. Do not clothe yourselves in solitude, as if you have already been justified, but coming together to the same place, inquire about the common benefit. For the scripture says: Woe to those who are wise in themselves and knowledgeable before themselves. Let us become spiritual, let us become a perfect temple to God. As long as it is in us, let us practice the fear of God and strive to keep his commandments, so that we may rejoice in his righteousness. The Lord will judge the world without respect of persons. Each one will receive according to what he has done. If he is good, his righteousness will precede him: if he is evil, the reward of evil will be before him: so that we may not, being at ease as called ones, be overcome by our sins, and the evil ruler, having taken authority over us, may cast us out of the kingdom of the Lord. And also, my brothers, consider this: when you see so many signs and wonders having occurred in Israel, and yet they have been abandoned: let us pay attention, lest, as it is written, many are called, but few are chosen.

bible_refs.note: Enoch is quoted as saying something about the perfect scandal
Daniel is quoted as saying something about the fourth beast

pass_b_english: We must therefore examine the present situation very carefully, searching out what can save us. Let us flee completely from every work of lawlessness, or the works of lawlessness will overtake us; and let us hate the deception of this present age, so that we may be loved in the age to come. We must not give our souls any rest, or they will gain the power to run alongside sinners and the wicked, and we will become like them. The perfect stumbling block has drawn near, the one written about, as Enoch says. For the Master has cut short the times and the days so that his beloved may hurry and come into the inheritance, and the prophet puts it this way: "Ten kingdoms will reign on the earth, and a little king will rise up behind them; he will humble three of the kings into one" (Enoch). Daniel speaks of the same thing: "I saw a fourth beast, evil and strong and more savage than all the beasts of the sea; from it ten horns arose, and from them a little horn, an offshoot, and it humbled three of the great horns into one" (Daniel). You ought to understand this. And I also ask you this, as one of you, loving all of you even more than my own soul: pay attention to yourselves right now, and do not imitate those who pile up their sins while claiming, "Their covenant is ours as well." It is ours, indeed, but they lost it in the end, even though they had already received it through Moses. For Scripture says: "Moses was on the mountain fasting forty days and forty nights, and he received the covenant from the Lord, stone tablets written with the finger of the Lord's hand" (Exod 34:28). But they turned back to idols and lost it. For the Lord says: "Moses, Moses, come down quickly, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly" (Exod 32:7). And Moses understood and threw the two tablets from his hands, and their covenant was shattered, so that the covenant of the beloved Jesus might be sealed in our hearts in the hope of his faith. Although I wanted to write many things, I did so not as a teacher but as one who loves, so that we would not fall short of what we possess; I have labored to write to you for your sake. Therefore let us be watchful in these last days: the whole time of our faith will not help us if we do not now, in this lawless time and amid the coming scandals, resist as befits sons of God, so that the evil one may not gain a foothold. Let us flee from all emptiness; let us utterly hate the works of the evil way. Do not retreat into solitude as though you were already justified, but gather together and seek the common good. For Scripture says: "Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and discerning in their own sight" (Isa 5:21). Let us become spiritual; let us become a perfect temple for God. As far as it lies within us, let us practice the fear of God and strive to keep his commandments, so that we may rejoice in his righteous judgments. The Lord will judge the world without partiality. Each person will receive according to what he has done: if he is good, his righteousness will go before him; if he is evil, the reward of evil will be before him. Let us not, while resting at ease as called ones, be overcome by our sins, and let the evil ruler not seize authority over us and cast us out of the kingdom of the Lord. And one more thing, my brothers: understand this: when you see so many signs and wonders that have taken place in Israel, and yet they have been abandoned, let us pay attention, lest, as it is written, we find that many are called but few are chosen (Matt 22:14).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the complex conditional and purpose clauses. Scripture citations in Pass B (Exod 34:28, Exod 32:7, Isa 5:21, Matt 22:14) correctly identify the biblical sources alluded to in the Greek. The distinction between the 'covenant of Moses' and the 'covenant of Jesus' is preserved. The nuances of 'without respect of persons' (ἀπροσωπολήμπτως) and the warnings against solitude/justification are correctly rendered.
